areas.description: A user-started collection with a cancellable progress notification that feeds the panel, diagnostics and status bar.
areas.title: On-demand scan

areas.description: Scans on startup, on a periodic timer and when the config file is saved, one at a time, staying quiet in folders with nothing configured.
areas.title: Automatic refresh

areas.description: Showing sources that failed during a run so a partial inventory never looks like a clean one, without repeating popups for automatic runs.
areas.title: Failed-source reporting

areas.description: Reading the CLI's JSON report into rows with stable identity, severity, days left and display names, kept as one fresh snapshot per workspace folder.
areas.title: Inventory snapshot

domains.description: Collecting the ranked expiry inventory by running expiry-radar and turning its results into what the editor shows.
domains.title: Scanning

areas.description: The default single list in priority order, with icons per severity, tooltips explaining each item and a notice at the top for failed sources.
areas.title: Ranked list

areas.description: Switching between grouping by rank and by kind, with groups ordered by worst deadline and an Expand All action.
areas.title: Grouping and expansion

areas.description: A multi-select filter by how close the deadline is and by item kind, where an empty axis means everything.
areas.title: Filtering

areas.description: The view badge and status bar summary counting what has expired or expires next.
areas.title: Attention indicators

areas.description: Per-row actions such as copying an item's details and context menus that depend on whether the item was recorded or discovered.
areas.title: Item actions

domains.description: The tree view and status bar where operators browse what is expiring, in blast-radius order.
domains.title: Inventory panel

areas.description: Editor diagnostics on declared hosts, domains and manual entries, with severity set by deadline and messages explaining the blast radius.
areas.title: Expiry squiggles

areas.description: Finding the exact line and column where each recorded item is declared, by scanning the config text rather than parsing it.
areas.title: Declaration lookup

domains.description: Linking expiring items back to the lines in expiry-radar.json that declared them.
domains.title: Config file insights

areas.description: A guided prompt sequence to record a host, domain or manual item, defaulting to the current selection and starting a scan right away.
areas.title: Add item

areas.description: Rejecting expiry dates and entries the CLI would refuse, and rendering each kind as the JSON the config expects.
areas.title: Entry validation

areas.description: Stopping tracking of a recorded item, after checking that the config line still names it.
areas.title: Remove item

areas.description: Adding entries to and removing them from the config file in place, creating a starter config from the repository example when none exists.
areas.title: Config file writing

domains.description: Recording and removing things to watch without hand-editing the config schema.
domains.title: Tracking items

areas.description: Showing the CLI's own self-contained HTML report in an editor tab, with a CSP, a bridge for external links and stale-report replacement.
areas.title: HTML report view

areas.description: Exporting the inventory to a file in a user-chosen output format.
areas.title: Report export

areas.description: Checking one host's certificate chain and domain registration right away without touching the config.
areas.title: Host probe

domains.description: One-off documents and answers produced outside the regular inventory refresh.
domains.title: Reports and probes

areas.description: Finding the expiry-radar binary in the usual locations and offering a one-click install when it is missing.
areas.title: CLI discovery and install

areas.description: A doctor command that checks the binary, the config, settings that shrink results and missing credentials for enabled sources.
areas.title: Environment check
